paper.title: A Latent Source Model for Online Collaborative Filtering

settings.name_in_paper: Latent source model for online recommendation
unmapped: n users each recommended one of m items per round; each item can be recommended to a given user at most once (consumed items become unavailable)
users belong to one of k latent types uniformly at random; users of the same type share an item preference vector p_u in [0,1]^m
ratings are +/-1 with like-probability p_ui, independent across items
objective is expected number of likable items (p_ui > 1/2) recommended, compared to an oracle recommending likable items first
learner (via threshold theta) needs the ambiguity margin Delta and incoherence gamma; k is not known
settings.definition_quote: We consider a system with $n$ users and $m$ items. At each time step, each user is recommended an item that she or he hasn't consumed yet, upon which, for simplicity, we assume that the user immediately consumes the item and rates it $+1$ (like) or $-1$ (dislike). ... we aim to maximize the expected number of \emph{likable} items recommended up to time $T$: r_+^{(T)} = \sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{u=1}^n \E[X_{ut}]

symbols.Delta_amb: ambiguity margin: |p_ui - 1/2| >= Delta for all u,i
symbols.mu: minimum fraction of likable items of any user

conditions: user types uniformly random among k
n = O(m^C) for some constant C>1

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Take as input to Collaborative-Greedy $\theta = 2 \Delta^2 (1 + \gamma)$ ... and $\alpha \in (0,4/7]$. Under the latent source model and assumptions A1 and A2, if the number of users $n=O(m^C)$ satisfies $n = \Omega(km \log \frac{1}{\delta} + (4/\delta)^{1/\alpha})$, then for any $\tc \le T \le \mu m$, the expected proportion of likable items recommended by Collaborative-Greedy up until time $T$ satisfies $\frac{r_+^{(T)}}{T n} \ge (1 - \frac{\tc}{T})(1-\delta)$

results.notes: Paper states a lower bound on the expected fraction of likable items; recorded as an upper bound on the shortfall T*n - r_+ relative to an oracle that recommends only likable items (multiplied through by T n). T_learn itself is a Theta expression. delta is a tolerance parameter, not a failure probability of a high-probability bound.

bound.regime: n >= max{8k log(4/delta), (4/delta)^(1/alpha)}; mu m >= t >= max{(2 log(10 k m n^alpha/Delta)/(Delta^4(1-gamma)^2))^(1/(1-alpha)), (20 log(96/delta)/(Delta^4(1-gamma)^2))^(1/(1-alpha)), (4/delta)^(1/alpha)}; n t^(1-alpha) >= 40 k m log(16m/delta)/Delta^2

symbols.X_ut: indicator that item recommended to user u at time t is likable

conditions: conditions on n, m, t as in regime

source.label: lem:general-conditions
source.quote: Let $\delta \in (0,1)$ be some pre-specified tolerance. If the number of users $n$ and items $m$ satisfy ... then $\P(X_{ut}=1) \ge 1 - \delta.$

results.notes: Per-round bound: probability of recommending an unlikable item at round t is at most delta. Expression records 1 - P(X_ut=1).
